How to tell: membership is voluntary, so the reason to stay must be a benefit. Economic collaboration is one of the main benefits members get.

Why not the others:
A. cultural assimilation: members keep their own cultures; assimilation, meaning taking on another people's culture, was a French colonial policy.
B. mandatory military assistance: the Commonwealth is not a military alliance and places no duty on members to give military help.
D. visa free policy: Commonwealth citizens generally need visas to visit many other member states, including Britain.

Exam tip: for questions on why a country belongs to a voluntary organisation, look for a practical benefit such as economic, technical or educational cooperation, and reject options with words like 'mandatory' or benefits the organisation does not actually give.

items.hint1: Recall why African leaders formed the OAU in 1963 and replaced it with the African Union in 2002. What did they want African states to have in their dealings with the rest of the world?
items.hint2: The AU works with other continents and with bodies such as the UN, so it does not block diplomacy. No regional body can stop globalisation from reaching its members.
items.hint3: Two options remain. Ask which one the AU can actually deliver, and which one it can only work towards without being able to guarantee it.
items.solution:
Answer: A. fosters regional unity and cooperation

The African Union, which replaced the OAU in 2002, exists to promote unity, solidarity and cooperation among African states. By acting together, members have a stronger voice in the international community, for example at the UN, than each would have alone.

How to tell: the question asks about the AU's significance in the international community. Its main value is bringing African states together to cooperate and speak as one.

Why not the others:
B. shields member countries from Globalization: no regional body can shut out globalisation; the AU tries to help members benefit from it.
C. protects member countries from Neo-colonialism: opposing neo-colonialism, meaning outside control through economic and indirect means, is part of its outlook, but it cannot guarantee protection, and many members still depend heavily on outside powers.
D. obstructs diplomatic engagement with other continent: the AU works with other continents and organisations; it does not block them.

Exam tip: for AU or OAU questions, anchor on unity and cooperation among African states, and reject options that promise complete protection or that make the organisation sound hostile to the outside world.

items.hint1: Civil society organisations are groups outside government, such as NGOs, trade unions and human rights groups. Think about how they link ordinary citizens to the business of government.
items.hint2: Civil society groups do more than one narrow thing, so be suspicious of any option that limits them with the word 'only'.
items.hint3: Two options remain. Democratic governance works within the law. Which of the two describes the broad, everyday work these groups do, rather than a tactic used only now and then?
items.solution:
Answer: C. facilitating citizen engagement and activism

Civil society organisations are non-governmental groups, such as NGOs, trade unions, professional bodies, religious groups and human rights groups, that stand between citizens and the state. They strengthen democracy by informing citizens, encouraging them to vote and speak up, monitoring elections and holding government to account.

How to tell: the correct option must describe a broad, lawful contribution. Getting citizens engaged and active in public affairs is the core of what these groups do.

Why not the others:
A. advancing sectoral interest only: some groups do push the interest of one sector, but 'only' ignores their wider role of involving citizens.
B. encouraging civil disobedience: civil society organisations work mainly through lawful means such as advocacy and peaceful protest, not by deliberately breaking the law.
D. setting political agenda only: they help shape what government discusses, but 'only' leaves out their main role.

Exam tip: when an option says 'only', test whether the group does anything else. If it does, the option is too narrow.
